messages:
sophie_sales: ACME enterprise POC stalled during security review + our demo; they report 401s and confused about scoping/IP controls. Can we triage quickly?
acme_infra: During the security call we tried our onboarding token and got 401 Invalid API key. Our security team also asked if keys can be scoped to a service account and if CIDR whitelisting is possible for hosted PoCs.
eli_se: Quick checklist: 1) are you calling `Authorization: Bearer <KEY>`? 2) what does the key prefix look like (`rwd-`, `rwd-test_`)? 3) any tenant headers or SDK envs set?
acme_infra: We used `Authorization: Bearer` and key starts with `rwd-sa_` (looks like a service account token). No extra headers in our demo script.
marta_platform: The `rwd-sa_` prefix indicates a service-account style key tied to an org with stricter rules. Can you run the same curl and paste the `x-rwd-request-id` from the response headers?
acme_infra: Response: `HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized`
body: `{"error":"Invalid API key"}`
header: `x-rwd-request-id: rwd-req-da7b1`
secrets_bot: secrets-service: lookup rwd-req-da7b1 -> key fingerprint found, status: active, key_type: service_account, bound_org: org-acme-enterprise, bound_project: prod, allowed_scopes: [inference:generate, embeddings:read], ip_allowlist: none, rotation_policy: org-default.
eli_se: Key is active and org-bound. Two likely causes: 1) the request is hitting a different tenant header (proxy/SDK) causing mismatch, or 2) the service account requires an additional header `X-RWD-SA: <sa-id>` in some enterprise setups. Do you have any custom headers?
acme_infra: We don't set `X-RWD-SA`. Our onboarding doc didn't mention that. Local dev tool (internal CLI) might add it though.
marta_platform: Some enterprise clients use short-lived SA tokens minted by an internal broker; the server expects either the SA header or that the key be used from approved IP blocks. Since your key shows no ip_allowlist, it's allowed from anywhere. We should check if the internal CLI is overwriting the Authorization header with a cached/old token.
acme_infra: How do we check token fingerprint vs the one in your secret store? We can't see the fingerprint locally.
secrets_bot: secrets-service: for key id `rwd-sa_83d` (fingerprint sha256:aa11) last_seen_request: rwd-req-da7b1, last_status: 401 from ip 198.51.100.23.
eli_se: If the IP is coming from a NATed corporate gateway that rewrites headers or inserts `X-RWD-Org-Id`, that could trigger a mismatch. Can you capture the full raw request from the demo environment including all headers?
acme_infra: Pasted raw headers from demo run: `Authorization: Bearer rwd-sa_83d`
`User-Agent: acme-demo/1.2`
`X-Forwarded-For: 198.51.100.23`
`X-RWD-Org-Id: org-acme-staging`
eli_se: There it is. `X-RWD-Org-Id` injected by the gateway and it doesn't match `org-acme-enterprise` bound to the key. That will make server reject with 403 normally, but given some internal routing it returned 401 in your case.
marta_platform: Immediate unblock options: (A) ask infra/security team to stop injecting `X-RWD-Org-Id` or map it to the correct org id, (B) create a short-lived PoC service key bound to `org-acme-staging` for the demo, or (C) generate a standard PoC key (non-SA) for quick demo. Which do you prefer?
sophie_sales: ACME wants the demo unblocked ASAP and also needs written answers for the security questionnaire about scoping and IP allowlisting. Recommend we provide short-lived key for demo and a security writeup.
acme_infra: Temp key would be fastest. Also please confirm whether hosted PoC supports per-key CIDR allowlist — security insisted on it.
marta_platform: Hosted public tier does not support per-key CIDR allowlist. CIDR/IP allowlist is available for Dedicated/Private customers; for hosted PoCs we recommend short TTL keys and service-account patterns as mitigation. We will document that for their security team.
secrets_bot: secrets-service: created key `rwd-test_sa_poc_27` bound_org: org-acme-staging, scopes: [inference:generate], key_type: test_service_account, expires: 48h, status: active, id: rwd-test_sa_poc_27.
acme_infra: Swapped in `rwd-test_sa_poc_27` and retried demo -> got 200 OK, response returned. Demo proceeds.
eli_se: I'll DM a short snippet showing how to detect injected tenant headers in the SDK and fail fast with a helpful log when mismatch detected. Also filing a tiny console UX ticket to surface "bound org" and "key type" next to keys.
sophie_sales: For the security questionnaire: we'll answer that hosted keys can be scope-limited and time-limited for PoCs; IP allowlists and enterprise KMS/HSM support are available on Dedicated/Private. We'll attach the created temp key id to the PoC record.
ops_bot: crm: updated PoC ACME-ENT-2026 with key `rwd-test_sa_poc_27`, note: demo unblocked, security writeup pending.
marta_platform: One more note: ACME reported intermittent 429s when running parallel embedding jobs during load test. Recommended defaults: begin at 40 req/min per client, batch embeddings into chunks of 8-16, use exponential backoff with full jitter on 429s, and watch `x-rwd-remaining` and `x-rwd-reset` headers for ramping.
acme_infra: Thanks all. We'll proceed with the demo and follow up on security doc. Closing swarm unless anything else pops. :white_check_mark:
